intro: MacroTrackr is AGPLv3. The whole tracker runs on your own hardware with a SQLite file and local accounts, with no external auth provider, no telemetry and no licence key. The managed service at macrotrackr.com runs the same code.

principles.title: The same build, either way
principles.description: Self-hosting is not a cut-down edition. Managed hosting adds cross-device sync and billing; everything else is identical, because it is the same image.

principles.title: Your data stays a file you own
principles.description: The backend stores everything in one SQLite database on a volume you mount. Back it up by copying a file. Export or delete it from Settings at any time.

principles.title: Nothing phones home
principles.description: Analytics and billing are disabled by default in self-hosted mode, and the billing routes are not mounted at all. There is no usage reporting to switch off.

principles.title: No accounts you did not create
principles.description: Self-hosted mode uses local authentication with database-backed sessions. It does not require Clerk, an OAuth provider, or any outbound connection to sign in.

platforms.name: Docker Compose
platforms.detail: The standard path. `docker compose up -d` with the published images from GitHub Container Registry.

platforms.name: Unraid
platforms.detail: Community Applications XML template, with appdata mapped to a path you choose.

platforms.name: CasaOS and ZimaOS
platforms.detail: Import the compose file as a custom app, or add the AppStore manifest to your own list.

platforms.name: Umbrel
platforms.detail: Community App Store manifest, installable from the CLI.

faqs.question: What does AGPLv3 mean for me?
faqs.answer: Run it, modify it and self-host it freely. If you distribute a modified version, or offer it to others over a network, that version has to be published under the same licence. Running an unmodified copy for yourself or your household carries no obligations.

faqs.question: Is the self-hosted version missing features?
faqs.answer: No. Meal logging, barcode scanning, macro goals, weekly trends, the importers and every calculator are in the open-source build. Managed hosting exists for cross-device sync and for people who would rather not run a server.

faqs.question: What does it need to run?
faqs.answer: A machine that runs Docker. It uses SQLite rather than a separate database server, so there is nothing else to provision, and it is comfortable on a NAS or a small VPS.

faqs.question: Can I move between self-hosted and managed later?
faqs.answer: Yes. Data export is in Settings, and the importers read the same format, so you can move in either direction without losing history.

faqs.question: Do I need an account to use the calculators?
faqs.answer: No. Every calculator on the site runs in the browser with no account and no data sent anywhere.
